slot.brief: Give four carbanions (methyl vs substituted/hybridised variations, e.g. sp3 vs sp2 vs sp C−) and ask to rank their stability.

stem: The correct decreasing order of stability of the following carbanions is: (I) $\text{CH}_3^-$, (II) $\text{HC}\equiv\text{C}^-$, (III) $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}^-$, (IV) $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}^-$

verdicts.working: Carbanion stability rises with s-character: sp (HC≡C⁻, II) > sp² (CH2=CH⁻, IV) > sp³. Among sp³, the +I effect of three methyl groups destabilizes (CH3)3C⁻ (III) relative to CH3⁻ (I). Order: II > IV > I > III, matching option B.

working:
The stability of carbanions is governed by two main factors: 1. Hybridization of the carbanionic carbon: As the percentage of $s$-character increases, the electronegativity of the carbon increases, allowing it to accommodate negative charge more effectively ($sp > sp^2 > sp^3$). In $\text{HC}\equiv\text{C}^-$ (II), the carbon is $sp$-hybridized ($50\%\ s$-character). In $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}^-$ (IV), the carbon is $sp^2$-hybridized ($33.3\%\ s$-character). In $\text{CH}_3^-$ (I) and $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}^-$ (III), the carbanionic carbons are $sp^3$-hybridized ($25\%\ s$-character). Thus: $\text{II} > \text{IV} > (\text{I}, \text{III})$. 2. Inductive effect ($+I$): Alkyl groups are electron-donating by $+I$ effect, which intensifies the negative charge on the carbanion and destabilizes it. The methyl carbanion $\text{CH}_3^-$ (I) has no alkyl groups, whereas the tert-butyl carbanion $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}^-$ (III) has three methyl groups exerting a destabilizing $+I$ effect. Thus: $\text{I} > \text{III}$. Combining both factors gives the overall decreasing order of stability: $\text{II} > \text{IV} > \text{I} > \text{III}$.

Independent check: Carbanion stability rises with s-character: sp (HC≡C⁻, II) > sp² (CH2=CH⁻, IV) > sp³. Among sp³, the +I effect of three methyl groups destabilizes (CH3)3C⁻ (III) relative to CH3⁻ (I). Order: II > IV > I > III, matching option B.

draft.distractor_notes:
Option A assumes the methyl carbanion ($sp^3$) is more stable than the vinyl carbanion ($sp^2$), neglecting the major stabilizing influence of $s$-character.
Option C reverses the order by mistakenly applying the stability order of carbocations ($3^\circ > 1^\circ > sp^2 > sp$) to carbanions.
Option D correctly applies hybridization but ranks the alkyl carbanions according to carbocation stability ($3^\circ > \text{methyl}$) rather than carbanion stability.
